timing: 8-way concurrent encodes (x265 default threads); wall clock from /usr/bin/time, second run of each cell. CPU-time cross-check ratio = 4.547. The box was shared with the sibling libsvtav1 bench for roughly the first hour of the encode phase; wall-clock times are contended, the slow/slower ratio is not expected to be biased because cells were shuffled so both presets experience the same load distribution.

machine is an old Xeon E5-2620 v2 (Ivy Bridge, AVX1 only, no AVX2): absolute encode times are not production-representative; only the slow/slower ratio and the matched-VMAF bitrate ratio are machine-independent.

matched-VMAF comparison is a BD-rate simplification: per material, linear fit of VMAF vs log10(kbps) over the 5 CRF anchors, solved at VMAF 95 when 95 lies inside the range common to both presets; when both presets stay above 95 at every anchor the lowest common VMAF is used, when neither preset reaches 95 the highest common VMAF is used (interpolation only, never extrapolation).
concurrency recorded in run_meta: encode_workers=8, vmaf_workers=8 (cap: never more than 8 ffmpeg processes at any time).
encode command locked to -c:v libx265 -crf <anchor> -preset <preset> with no lookahead/tune/multipass/aq; x265 thread pool left at default (auto).
this bench is partial/pre-run only for the preset axis; D1 anchor axis (CRF 20 vs 16) is not measured here (see Plan v3 12.3).
